subject: science
passage: Not all movement along geological faults is sudden. In slow slip events, first detected around 2000 by networks of GPS stations in the Pacific Northwest and Japan, sections of a fault creep over days or weeks, releasing as much energy as a sizable earthquake yet producing no violent shaking. Seismologists initially regarded such events as a benign alternative to earthquakes, a way for faults to ______ stress harmlessly. Some now suspect the relationship is less reassuring: a slow slip can transfer stress to neighboring, locked portions of a fault and may, in some cases, hasten the very ruptures it once seemed to forestall.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The initial view saw slow slip as a "benign alternative to earthquakes": the fault releases energy gently instead of violently. The blank must mean "release and get rid of." The later concern, that slip passes stress to other parts of the fault, is what the newer view adds.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Accumulate" means build up; the text says slow slip releases energy, and building up stress would not be harmless.
explanation.B: Correct. "Dissipate" means release and scatter until it is gone, which fits the early view of slow slip as a harmless release of stress.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Passing stress to neighboring sections is the worrying possibility the newer view raises; the original "benign" view saw slow slip as getting rid of stress, not passing it on.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The events release energy measurable by GPS; nothing suggests they hide stress.
